tagline: A shore loop out to the lighthouses at the river's mouth.
intro: From the Post Road at Saybrook Manor, Route 154 heads south on Great Hammock Road, runs along the Sound as Plum Bank Road, turns east through Knollwood and comes into Fenwick past the golf course and across South Cove. Then it swings west as College Street and Main Street and turns north past North Cove to the town center, six miles all told.

The Saybrook Colony was planted at the mouth of the Connecticut River in late 1635, with Colonel George Fenwick and Captain Lion Gardiner among its leaders. In 1701 the Collegiate School was chartered here, and moved to New Haven in 1716 to become Yale.

moments.title: Fenwick
moments.text: Connecticut's least populous borough, 53 people in 2020, is mostly Shingle-style houses around a nine-hole golf course, and Katharine Hepburn died at the family home here in 2003.

moments.title: Lynde Point lighthouses
moments.text: The brownstone Inner Light of 1838 at the tip of Lynde Point and the sparkplug Outer Light on the breakwater mark the river channel, the outer one familiar from Connecticut license plates.

moments.title: Old Saybrook
moments.text: Here the colonists' fort burned mysteriously in 1647, and the mound of its successor lasted until 1871, when the Valley Railroad leveled it for fill across the coves.
